conventions.convention: All group actions on these pages are left actions; for subsets, g·B={g·b:b∈B}. A block is required to be nonempty, and the page defines a block system as a partition into blocks.
Primitive and imprimitive are defined only for transitive actions; primitive means that only the singleton partition and the one-block partition are block systems.
For k≥1, k-transitivity concerns ordered k-tuples of pairwise distinct points, while k-homogeneity concerns k-element subsets.
The rank of a transitive action is the number of orbits of a chosen point stabilizer; those orbits are suborbits and their cardinalities are subdegrees.
The imprimitive wreath product uses (k·f)(σ)=f(k⁻¹·σ) on H^Σ and (f,k)·(b,σ)=(f(k·σ)·b,k·σ) on B×Σ.
The commutator convention is [g,h]=ghg⁻¹h⁻¹.
Metric properness means finiteness of every transporter between bounded subsets; coboundedness means that the translates of one bounded subset cover the space.
A geometric action is isometric, proper, and cobounded in the metric-action convention of this page.
The growth function starts on n∈ℕ and counts the closed word-metric ball of radius n about the identity.
For nondecreasing f,g:ℕ→ℕ, f≼g means that some natural C≥1 satisfies f(n)≤C·g(Cn+C)+C for every n; f≃g means mutual comparison.
Polynomial growth means β≼n^d for some integer d≥0; exponential means a^n≼β for some real a>1; subexponential means not exponential; intermediate means subexponential but not polynomial.
For a finitely generated nilpotent group of class c, the homogeneous dimension is D(G)=Σ_{i=1}^c i·rank_Z(γ_i(G)/γ_{i+1}(G)); the trivial group has class 0 under the published nilpotency convention.
The modern Kan-extension orientation is used: a left Kan extension has η:F⇒LK and is initial among such pairs; a right Kan extension has ε:RK⇒F and is terminal.
A functor category [C,E] is formed as a category only when the source C is small; a large-source occurrence is only metatheoretic shorthand under the library's size policy.
Pointwise left Kan extensions use colimits over (K↓d), and pointwise right Kan extensions use limits over (d↓K); the legs indexed by identity arrows are respectively η_c and ε_c.
The representable-preservation definition uses covariant representables E(e,−) for right Kan extensions and passes to opposites, equivalently using E(−,e), for left Kan extensions.
An absolute Kan extension is one preserved by every functor out of its codomain, not merely by representables.
A dense subcategory is represented by a fully faithful i:A→C with A small and C locally small such that 1_C is the pointwise left Kan extension of i along itself.
The codensity monad comes from a right self-Kan extension ε:TG⇒G; η and μ are the unique transformations satisfying 1_G=ε∘(ηG) and ε∘(μG)=ε∘(Tε).
Filters are proper: the empty set is excluded. An ultrafilter is maximal under inclusion among those proper filters.

load_bearing.statement: Let C,D,E be categories, K:C→D and F:C→E. A left Kan extension is a functor L:D→E with η:F⇒LK such that every α:F⇒MK factors uniquely as α=(ᾱK)∘η; a right Kan extension is a functor R:D→E with ε:RK⇒F such that every β:MK⇒F factors uniquely as β=ε∘(β̄K).

For fixed d, a colimit of the diagram on (K↓d) has the objectwise universal property of the left Kan extension value, and a limit of the diagram on (d↓K) has the objectwise universal property of the right Kan extension value. Supplied choices for every d assemble into Lan_K F and Ran_K F, with unit and counit components given by the identity-indexed legs.
A nonempty subset B⊆Ω is a block if for every g∈G either g·B=B or (g·B)∩B=∅. A block system is a partition of Ω into blocks.
For a finitely generated group G and finite generating set S, β_{G,S}:ℕ→ℕ is β_{G,S}(n)=|{g∈G:|g|_S≤n}|, the cardinality of the closed word-metric ball of radius n about the identity.

A left Kan extension (L,η) is pointwise when, for every d, the maps L(u)∘η_c indexed by (c,u:Kc→d) form a colimit cocone over (K↓d). A right Kan extension (R,ε) is pointwise when, for every d, the maps ε_c∘R(u) indexed by (c,u:d→Kc) form a limit cone over (d↓K).

An action is isometric when every group element preserves distance, proper when every transporter {(g):(g·B)∩C≠∅} between bounded B,C is finite, and cobounded when the translates of some bounded B cover X.
A transitive action is primitive if its only block systems are the singleton partition and the one-block partition; it is imprimitive if it is transitive and not primitive.
For nondecreasing f,g:ℕ→ℕ, f≼g if some natural C≥1 satisfies f(n)≤C·g(Cn+C)+C for every n; f≃g if both f≼g and g≼f.
For k≥1, an action is k-transitive if every ordered k-tuple of pairwise distinct points can be sent to every other such tuple, and k-homogeneous if every k-element subset can be sent to every other.
An action of a group on a metric space is geometric if it is isometric, proper, and cobounded.

Let G act geometrically on a geodesic metric space X, and fix x₀∈X. Then G is finitely generated. More precisely, for the finite generating set S={g:d_X(x₀,g·x₀)≤2D+1} obtained from the preceding lemma, the orbit map (G,d_S)→X is a quasi-isometry.

If K:C→D is fully faithful, then every unit component F(c)→L(Kc) of a pointwise left Kan extension along K is an isomorphism, and every counit component R(Kc)→F(c) of a pointwise right Kan extension is an isomorphism.

For small C and a presheaf P:C^op→Set, P is the colimit of the diagram ∫P→[C^op,Set] sending (c,x) to y(c). Equivalently, cocones from that diagram to Q are in bijection with natural transformations P⇒Q.
Given a right Kan extension ε:TG⇒G of G along itself, the codensity monad has unit η uniquely determined by 1_G=ε∘(ηG) and multiplication μ uniquely determined by ε∘(μG)=ε∘(Tε).
For every finite generating set S of a finitely generated nilpotent group G, β_{G,S}(n)≃n^{D(G)}. This formula is recorded but not proved here.

concerns.concern: The forward implication is false under the preceding definition, which calls any partition into blocks a block system but does not require the partition to be G-invariant. In the regular action of C4, {{0,2},{1},{3}} is a partition into blocks, yet translation by 1 sends related points 0,2 to points 1,3 lying in different parts. Step 2.1 also incorrectly treats g·B as necessarily a member of the original partition.

The Statement is false for the page's definition of block system. The same regular C4 partition {{0,2},{1},{3}} is a block system as defined but has block sizes 2,1,1. Step 2.1 assumes that the translate g·B is a member of the chosen partition, which has not been required.

[L1] attributes to ex-natural-actions-of-symmetric-and-alternating-groups that A_n is a nontrivial normal subgroup of S_n and that the S_n action is primitive. The cited example states only the transitivity degrees of the natural S_n and A_n actions, so the dependency citation does not carry the two facts used by the refutation.

The displayed constant M=max_{s∈S∪S⁻¹}d(x₀,s·x₀) is undefined when G is trivial and S is the empty finite generating set, which the published finitely-generated-group definition permits. This is a boundary defect in the Statement, not merely a missing proof sentence.

The Statement defines S using 2D+1 without first quantifying D or stating that D is a coboundedness constant. D appears only later in Facts & Assumptions, so the more precise part of the theorem is not well-formed as written.

For an element g fixing x₀, the proof has ℓ=0 and chooses the least m with ℓ≤m, hence m=0 under the library's natural-number convention. The expression iℓ/m is then undefined, and arranging g₀=e=g_m forces g=e. A reader closes this immediately by treating ℓ=0 separately: then g∈S already.

The proof's load-bearing [A1] is the Bass–Guivarch formula, but [A1] contains no wikilink or source attribution, and the proof contract records only [L2], omitting [A1]. The frontmatter lists rem-bass-guivarch-growth-degree-formula, but the numbered proof does not identify that dependency.

The final inference uses the external Bass–Guivarch theorem as [A1], but [A1] has no link or source attribution and is absent from the contract's citations. Thus the growth-degree conclusion rests on an unaccounted numbered assumption despite the correct dependency appearing in frontmatter.

The second paragraph says the backward implication of Gromov's equivalence is separated out as cor-finitely-generated-nilpotent-groups-have-polynomial-growth. That corollary treats nilpotent groups, not virtually nilpotent groups; a finite-index/quasi-isometry argument is still needed. The prose therefore overstates what the cited local corollary establishes.

The Statement “Iwasawa's criterion needs only transitivity” does not specify which hypotheses of the criterion are retained or state a definite weakened theorem. The witness shows that primitivity supplies a normal-subgroup transitivity step, but the false claim itself remains meta-level and imprecise.

The Statement uses “uniformly comparable” without defining the comparison inequality or quantifying a uniform constant. The example clearly gives unbounded ratios, but the refuted proposition should state that precise conclusion.

Step 1.1 says that under the trivial action on (0,1), “its single orbit already covers the space.” Every orbit is actually a singleton. Coboundedness is still immediate by taking the bounded subset B=(0,1), whose orbit-union is B, so this is a locally closable proof-step error.
The item is a meta-claim about what this page proves rather than mathematical content, contrary to the direct-prose rule. Its refutation merely reads the proved_here marker.

The dependency def-prime declares a forward reference. Under the library's inherited-forward-reference mechanism, citing it makes this much later corollary inherit a sky forward marker to material already far below this page, producing a misleading reader-facing dependency marker even though the mathematics is sound.
